extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on conducting, recording, and handling interviews during patent prosecution (including video exhibits and grouped interviews) and the rules/format for making amendments to specifications, claims, and drawings under 37 CFR and MPEP. Covers examiner and applicant responsibilities, required forms (PTOL‑413/PTOL‑413B), timing limits, and special situations (final rejection, allowance, reissue, reexamination, provisional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Video tape viewing during interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys or applicants wishing to show a video tape during an examiner interview must demonstrate that the content of the video tape has a bearing on an outstanding issue in the application and its viewing will advance prosecution; prior approval by the supervisory patent examiner is required and use of the room/equipment must be granted by the Training Manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be made at least 1 week in advance to allow scheduling. Office video tape equipment (VHS and UHS) is available only in Patent Academy facilities (Crystal Square Four, Suite 700). Applicants should not contact the Patent Academy directly; scheduling of rooms and equipment must be done through and by the examiner conducting the interview. The substance of the interview, including a summary of the video tape content, must be made of record (see MPEP §713.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance of any interview must be made of record
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete written statement as to the substance of any face‑to‑face, video conference, electronic mail or telephone interview with regard to the merits of an application must be made of record in the application, whether or not an agreement was reached (37 CFR 1.133(b), MPEP §713.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reconsideration is requested in view of an interview, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the applicant. An interview does not remove the necessity for replies to Office actions as specified in §§1.111 and 1.135. All business should ordinarily be transacted in writing; oral promises or stipulations receive no attention if there is disagreement or doubt unless recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for examiner‑initiated interview summaries (PTOL‑413B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant responsibility to make the substance of an interview of record is excepted where the interview was initiated by the examiner and the examiner indicated on PTOL‑413B that the examiner will provide a written summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner initiates the interview and completes PTOL‑413B appropriately, the examiner's completed PTOL‑413B is considered a proper interview summary record and the applicant need not provide the interview record. The examiner is responsible to correct material inaccuracies which bear directly on patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must complete Interview Summary (PTOL‑413) when substantive matters discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must complete an Interview Summary form PTOL‑413 for each interview where a matter of substance has been discussed by checking appropriate boxes and filling blanks; if examiner initiated and PTOL‑413B is used, PTOL‑413 is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a personal interview, the duplicate copy of PTOL‑413 (with attachments) is given to the applicant at conclusion; for telephonic/email/video interviews, copy is mailed to correspondence address with or prior to next official communication, and may be faxed at conclusion. If a complete interview record is incorporated in an examiner's amendment, completion of PTOL‑413 may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTOL‑413 required information items
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTOL‑413 form provides for recordation of: (A) application number; (B) name of applicant; (C) name of examiner; (D) date of interview; (E) type of interview (personal, telephonic, electronic mail or video conference); (F) name of participant(s); (G) indication whether an exhibit was shown or demonstration conducted; (H) identification of claims discussed; (I) identification of specific prior art discussed; (J) indication whether an agreement was reached and description of general nature of agreement; (K) signature of examiner who conducted the interview; (L) names of other USPTO personnel present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL‑413 also contains a statement reminding the applicant of his/her responsibility to record the substance of the interview. The form must be given an appropriate paper number, placed in the right hand portion of the file, and listed on the file wrapper contents list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum contents required for a complete interview record
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete and proper recordation of the substance of any interview should include at least the applicable items: (A) brief description of any exhibit shown or demonstration; (B) identification of claims discussed; (C) identification of specific prior art discussed; (D) identification of principal proposed substantive amendments discussed (unless already described on PTOL‑413); (E) general thrust of principal arguments of applicant and examiner (need not be verbatim or highly detailed); (F) general indication of any other pertinent matters discussed; (G) if appropriate, general results or outcome of the interview; (H) for e‑mail interviews, a paper copy of the e‑mail MUST be made and placed in the patent application file as required by the Federal Records Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of arguments is sufficient if the general nature or thrust can be understood in file context; applicants may provide fuller descriptions of arguments they believe persuasive. An Interview Summary alone will not be a complete record unless it includes or is supplemented to include all applicable items above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing and timing of Interview Summary copies
rubrics_metrics.description: In personal interviews, duplicate PTOL‑413 is given at conclusion; for telephonic/e‑mail/video interviews, copy mailed to applicant's correspondence address with or prior to next official communication and may be faxed at conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional correspondence from the examiner is unlikely before allowance, the Interview Summary should be mailed promptly after the telephonic/electronic/video interview rather than with the next official communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review and accuracy check of applicant's interview summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are expected to carefully review the applicant's record of the substance of an interview. If the record is not complete or accurate, the examiner may give the applicant a 1‑month time period to complete the reply under 37 CFR 1.135(c) where the record is in reply to a nonfinal Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inaccuracy bears directly on patentability, the examiner should point it out in the next Office letter. If the claims are allowable for other reasons of record, the examiner should send a letter setting forth his/her version of the statement attributed to him/her. If record is complete and accurate, examiner should mark 'Interview record OK' with date and initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prior to first official action — limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing no interview is permitted, though examiner may indicate field of search to an attorney/searcher/inventor. A request for an interview prior to the first Office action is ordinarily granted in continuing or substitute applications; requests in other applications before the first action are untimely and will not be acknowledged if written, or granted if oral (37 CFR 1.133(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited amount of time may be spent indicating field of search. Applicants should not expect interviews before first Office action except in the specified continuing/substitute contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search in group requires consent of primary examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Search in the Technology Center art unit should be permitted only with the consent of a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conduct group searches without primary examiner's agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will not act as expounder of patent law or counselor
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office cannot act as an expounder of the patent law, nor as a 'counselor' for individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should not be used to obtain legal counseling or broad expositions of the law from Office personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews solely to 'sound out' the examiner are not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews that are solely for the purpose of 'sounding out' the examiner, such as by a local attorney acting for an out‑of‑town attorney, should not be permitted when any agreement would be conditional upon being satisfactory to the principal attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner discretion should be exercised to deny such interviews when they are merely exploratory without binding authority present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to conduct interviews — who may be granted interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are not normally granted to persons who lack proper authority from the applicant or attorney/agent of record on file, or who do not have a copy of the application file. A mere power to inspect is not sufficient authority for granting an interview involving the merits. Office employees are forbidden to hold communication with unregistered or suspended attorneys or agents unless that attorney/agent is the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered local representatives known to be the attorney's local representatives may be granted interviews even without a power of attorney on record in urgent situations. For telephone interviews by practitioners not of record, filing a facsimile of a power of attorney prior to the interview is recommended; otherwise the examiner may conduct the telephone interview with the Office file closed, working solely from the practitioner's file. Generally interviews should not be granted unless the requesting party has authority to bind the principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouped interviews practice for remote attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: For attorneys remote from Washington, D.C., grouped in‑person or video conference interviews are effective; if prearranged with agreement to file a prompt supplemental amendment to put the case in condition for concluding action, prompt filing of that amendment gives the application special status and immediate special action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use grouped interviews when practical to coordinate participants and accelerate prosecution by filing agreed supplemental amendments promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: No inter partes questions discussed ex parte
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not discuss inter partes questions ex parte with any of the interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid discussing issues that belong to inter partes proceedings in ex parte interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect exposure of other cases during interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an interview in the examiner's room, the examiner should arrange the desk so that all files, drawings and other papers, except those necessary for the interview, are placed out of view (see MPEP §101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure confidentiality and prevent inadvertent exposure of unrelated applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrations, exhibits, and models rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention may be exhibited or demonstrated during an interview by a model. A model received by the examiner which complies with 37 CFR 1.91 and is made part of the application record must be properly recorded on the 'Contents' portion of the application file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a model/exhibit is used solely for demonstration and not made part of the record (does not comply with 37 CFR 1.91), a full description of what was demonstrated/exhibited must be made of record (37 CFR 1.133(b)). Demonstrations of apparatus too large to bring into the Office may be viewed by the examiner outside the Office with supervisory approval. It is presumed witnessing the demonstration is essential to clarifying issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final rejection — limitations and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, one interview after final rejection is permitted. Prior to the interview, the intended purpose and content should be presented briefly, preferably in writing. Such an interview may be granted if the examiner is convinced disposal or clarification for appeal may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews merely to restate arguments of record or to discuss new limitations requiring more than nominal reconsideration or new search should be denied. A second or further interview after final rejection may be held if it will expedite issues for appeal or disposal. Interviews may be held after the shortened statutory period and prior to the maximum 6‑month period without extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after application sent to issue or after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is sent to issue (37 CFR 1.312) it is technically no longer under the primary examiner's jurisdiction; interviews involving detailed consideration of claims sought to be entered and prior art discussion for allowability should not be given. Requests for interviews on cases where a notice of allowance has been mailed should be granted only with specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a showing in writing of extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant is not entitled to greater consideration for informally presented amendments than for formally presented amendments; consideration of an amendment under 1.312 cannot be demanded as a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must be made by filing a paper in compliance with §1.52
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in applications (other than reissue) are made by filing a paper in compliance with §1.52 directing that specified amendments be made (37 CFR 1.121(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed amendment paper format and filing requirements; see further MPEP §714 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to specification — replacement paragraphs/sections and substitute specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification (other than claims/listings) may be made by instruction to delete/replace/add a paragraph, by replacement section, or by submitting a substitute specification, subject to requirements: replacement/added paragraphs/sections/substitute specification must be provided in clean form and accompanied by a marked‑up version showing changes relative to the previous version (37 CFR 1.121(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clean form = no markings to indicate changes. The marked‑up version is required as an aid to the examiner and must be based on the immediate previous version of record. Paragraphs should be unambiguously identified (paragraph number, page/line, or other method). Deleted matter can only be reinstated by a subsequent amendment presenting the previously deleted matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter permitted in amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application (37 CFR 1.121(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all amendments are supported by the original disclosure or earlier‑entered amendments; reinstatement of deleted matter requires prior presence in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to claims — rewriting, clean form, marked‑up versions, and status parentheticals
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to a claim must be made by rewriting the claim with all changes included. A rewritten or newly added claim must be submitted in clean form. If a claim is amended by rewriting with the same number, the amendment must be accompanied by a marked‑up version (separate) showing changes relative to the previous version and a parenthetical expression following the claim number indicating status (e.g., 'amended,' 'twice amended,' 'new') for both clean and marked‑up versions (37 CFR 1.121(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A canceled claim may be reinstated only as a new claim with a new claim number. A clean version of the entire set of pending claims may be submitted in a single amendment paper, which will be construed as canceling previous versions. Marked‑up versions are required only for claims being changed by the current amendment; added or canceled claims need not have marked‑up versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format recommendation for amendment paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended format for amendment paper: (A) a clean version of the amended (replacement) paragraph(s)/claim(s); (B) a remarks section beginning on a separate sheet; and (C) a marked‑up version (also on a separate sheet) showing changes and clearly identified as 'Version with markings to show changes made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following this order aids examiner review and complies with the revised amendment practice requirements effective after March 1, 2001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to application drawings must be submitted on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner. Upon approval, new drawings complying with §1.84 including the changes must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use red to indicate proposed changes on the separate paper; do not submit new drawings without examiner approval and compliance with §1.84.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings (37 CFR 1.121(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may be required to align claims, spec, and drawings; ensure consistency to avoid Office‑required corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for examiner's amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, including the claims, of an application made by the Office in an examiner's amendment may be made by specific instructions to insert or delete subject matter set forth in the examiner's amendment by identifying the precise point where insertion or deletion is to be made; compliance with the standard applicant amendment format is not required for examiner's amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's amendments follow a distinct procedure; applicants should review examiner's specified insert/delete instructions for incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for reissue, reexamination, and provisional amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in reissue applications must be made in accordance with §1.173. Proposed amendments to description and claims in patents involved in reexamination (ex parte §1.510 and inter partes §1.913) must comply with §1.530(d)‑(j). Amendments in provisional applications are not normally made; if made, they must comply with §1.121 and will be placed in the provisional application file but may not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the cited specific regulatory provisions for these special proceedings; provisional amendments are treated differently and may not be entered.
